goal: Add the missing admin_halt writer: an AAL2-gated admin route plus a Business detail panel that apply the Halt latch to a location's current Send batch, reusing the owner arm's latch mechanics and recording the RepWorth operator in account_audit_log.
non_goals: No migration — every value this needs already exists in migrations 091 and 108.
No new halt_reason CHECK member and no widening of OwnerHaltReason: the write union stays 2 members, the read union HaltReason stays 5.
No resume, undo or un-halt surface — the Halt latch stays monotone.
No cross-account /admin/solicitation list page; the surface is scoped to one location.
No change to the owner-facing Requests panel copy — the admin_halt read side already ships.
Not implementing the other two Halt latch writers (send_window_elapsed, batch_expired) or the #630 releaser.
The admin surface never renders customer outreach subjects or bodies.
Not re-opening #858: closeBatchIfSettled already canonicalises its own batch id as of PR #868.

NOT fixing haltBatch's identical pending-batch hole (plan review round 1, finding 2). The owner arm also permits halting a batch with built_at IS NULL, which makes batch-builder's later built_at stamp violate 091's halt-consistency CHECK. The admin arm refuses that state; changing the OWNER arm is a user-visible behaviour change this intake does not name, so it is logged for a follow-up ticket at step 8 instead of fixed here.
user_visible_behavior: An admin viewing /admin/businesses/[id] sees the location's current Send batch, its Batch state, how many Outreach rows a stop would cancel, and how many are already sending or sent.
When that batch is haltable, the admin can stop it, supplying a required free-text note.
Stopping writes halt_reason='admin_halt' and halted_by = the acting admin's users.id, and cancels that batch's rendered and queued Outreach rows.
The owner's Requests panel then renders the already-shipped copy: 'RepWorth support stopped this batch. It cannot be resumed — get in touch if that was not expected.'
An admin who has not stepped up to AAL2 is refused with 403 mfa_required and nothing is written.
A second stop on the same batch is a no-op reported as already_halted, with no second audit row and no second spine step.
A batch that is already closed, or still building, is refused as not_haltable; the panel shows no stop control for it.
invariants: The Halt latch is monotone: the CAS on halted_at IS NULL means a second halt writes nothing.
Outreach rows in 'sending' are NEVER cancelled — halt means 'no further sends', not 'undo'. Only 'rendered' and 'queued' are cancelled.
The latch never terminalizes the Send batch parent directly; it calls closeBatchIfSettled like every other terminal writer, so parent terminalization keeps one owner.
halt_reason is fixed by the route's identity. No request field can name it, in either arm.
OwnerHaltReason stays exactly {'owner_veto','owner_halt'} and LatchHaltReason is never exported; the admin arm cannot spell an owner reason and the owner arm cannot spell admin_halt.
writeAccountAuditLog runs in the SAME transaction as the latch write (CLAUDE.md 'Audit writes'), and BEFORE the run-spine calls; never a raw INSERT INTO account_audit_log.
Lock order stays advisory batch lock -> solicitation_batches row -> agent_runs: every run-spine call (recordStep, closeBatchIfSettled) happens LAST.

ADMIN ARM ONLY: adminHaltBatch never latches a batch with built_at IS NULL, so batch-builder's later built_at stamp cannot violate 091's halt-consistency CHECK. haltBatch keeps the identical hole on purpose — see the matching non_goal; stating this invariant unqualified would contradict that carve-out.
Invariant #15: src/lib/solicitation/approval.ts receives its DB client as an explicit parameter and never imports @/lib/db/server.
Invariant #12: the admin route parses, gates and maps errors only — the latch write lives in the domain module.
Invariant #8: the admin route proves tenancy with body-supplied accountId + businessId; a mismatched triple is the uniform 404, indistinguishable from an unknown batch.
The admin arm is NOT gated on SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED: support must be able to stop a stranded batch after the lane flag is turned off. The flag is a lane switch, not an authorization.
edge_cases: Mixed-case batch id from the request: canonicalised at the public entry point before the batch row is locked, so every later TEXT-key consumer including closeBatchIfSettled receives the canonical id.
Batch already halted -> already_halted, no second latch write, no second audit row, no second spine step.
Batch already closed -> not_haltable with the derived Batch state.

Batch still building (built_at IS NULL, state 'pending') -> not_haltable. Latching it would make batch-builder's later built_at stamp violate 091's (halted_at IS NULL OR built_at IS NULL OR halted_at >= built_at) CHECK and throw.
Parentless batch (all-withheld, generation never minted a Send batch parent) -> still latches, skips the spine step, still calls closeBatchIfSettled.
Real batch id under the wrong accountId or businessId -> not_found (404), same as an unknown id.
Admin authenticated but AAL1 -> 403 mfa_required, no write.
Caller with a non-admin role but a valid AAL2 session -> refused by the role gate, no write.
Batch in 'sending' with rows mid-flight -> those 'sending' rows survive, the join returns not_settled and the Send batch parent stays running.
writeAccountAuditLog throws -> the latch write and the outreach cancellations roll back with it, and no spine call happens.
Missing, empty or over-long (>1000 char) note -> 400 invalid_request, no write.
Body carrying reason / haltReason / halt_reason -> 400 from z.strictObject, and adminHaltBatch is never called.
Cross-origin POST -> refused by withSameOrigin before the gate.
SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED off -> the admin route still halts (D5).
Location has no batch at all -> the panel renders the no-batch state and no stop control.

adminHaltBatch leaves the send parent running while a sending outreach row remains live
adminHaltBatch cancels rendered and queued outreach rows with disposition_reason admin_halt
adminHaltBatch records solicitation_batch_admin_halted with the note, actor, entity, location, state_at_halt and cancelled_count
adminHaltBatch rolls back the latch, the outreach cancellations and the audit row when writeAccountAuditLog fails
adminHaltBatch writes its audit row before recordStep and closeBatchIfSettled, on the same transaction
adminHaltBatch delegates parent settlement to closeBatchIfSettled and never updates agent_runs directly
adminHaltBatch still calls closeBatchIfSettled for a parentless batch
adminHaltBatch halts a batch addressed by a mixed-case id and closes its send parent
adminHaltBatch returns not_found for a real batch id under the wrong tenant
adminHaltBatch returns not_haltable for a closed batch
adminHaltBatch returns not_haltable for an unbuilt pending batch and leaves the builder able to stamp built_at
readAdminBatchSummary returns the latest tenant-scoped batch with correct cancellable, sending and sent counts
readAdminBatchSummary returns only the admin-safe projection and never serializes an outreach subject or body
readAdminBatchSummary returns null for a real batch under the wrong account or business
haltBatch still derives owner_veto and owner_halt after the latch extraction
type contract: OwnerHaltReason is exactly owner_veto | owner_halt and LatchHaltReason is not exported
invariants: halting is a fixed point and preserves every outreach status except rendered and queued for arbitrary outreach-status multisets
the admin halt route refuses a caller without AAL2 step-up and writes nothing
the admin halt route refuses a non-admin caller even with an AAL2 session and writes nothing
the admin halt route rejects reason, haltReason and halt_reason as unknown fields and never calls adminHaltBatch
the admin halt route rejects a missing, empty or over-long note and writes nothing
the admin halt route rejects a cross-origin POST before calling adminHaltBatch
the admin halt route maps halted and already_halted to 200, not_haltable to 409 and not_found to 404
the admin halt route has no SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED gate — it halts with the send lane flag off
the admin halt panel shows a stop control for a haltable batch and submits the required note

the admin halt panel distinguishes sending outreach from the rendered and queued outreach a stop will cancel
the business detail page reads the admin batch summary sequentially without Promise.all
rollback_plan: Revert the PR. There is no migration to undo and no feature flag to flip — admin_halt is already a permitted CHECK member, so reverting simply removes the only writer and returns the value to unreachable. Any admin_halt rows already written stay valid and keep rendering the shipped owner copy; the Halt latch is monotone, so nothing needs unwinding. No staging or prod schema action at promotion.
observability: One account_audit_log row per successful halt: event_type='solicitation_batch_admin_halted', actor_user_id = the admin, entity_type='solicitation_batch', entity_id = the batch id, location_id = the business id, payload carrying the note, the derived Batch state at halt and the cancelled count. This is the durable 'a RepWorth operator did this' record.
One agent_run_steps row with step_key='batch_halted' and detail.halt_reason='admin_halt' on the Send batch parent — the batch-side story, absent only for a parentless batch.
A structured route log line naming status, batchId, businessId and cancelledCount — ids and counts only, never rendered subject or body.
Failures surface through internalError() as a 500 with a structured console.error, which reaches Sentry.
How I would know it broke: an admin_halt batch with no matching account_audit_log row, or a solicitation_outreach row still in 'rendered'/'queued' on a batch whose halted_at is set.
